title: Summer Walker in Legal Dispute With Interscope Over Record Deal
summary: Walker invoked California's seven-year statute to terminate her contract with Interscope. The label has now responded with a lawsuit.
body: Summer Walker and Interscope Records are in a legal dispute over the status of her record deal. Walker, who signed a joint deal with the Universal Music Group (UMG) subsidiary and label/management company LVRN in 2017, sent a notice of termination to Interscope in August. Interscope responded on Friday (Oct. 9) by submitting a lawsuit, obtained and first reported by Billboard , alleging that if Walker does indeed break their deal, she’d owe $50 million for not yet delivering all her promised albums. Related Summer Walker Completes No. 1 Trilogy on Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums Chart Hilary Duff to Receive Outstanding Pop Tour of the Year Award at 2026 Billboard Live Music Summit Judge Rules Woman Accused of Shooting at Rihanna & A$AP Rocky's Home Mentally Fit to Stand Trial The singer-songwriter is invoking California’s “seven-year statute,” a 1944 state law that allows an individual to exit a personal services contract after that amount of time. The statute was amended in 1987 to allow record labels to sue artists for damages if they leave after seven years but before fulfilling all their album commitments. title: Survey suggests that the iPhone Duo is tempting a surprising number of Android fans
summary: Not quite an Android exodus, but encouraging reading for Apple.
body: Credit: Apple Apple may have arrived years late to the foldable phone party, but it’s certainly made an impression with the iPhone Duo. The company’s first foldable has a near-creaseless display, some interesting software tricks, and a $1,999 price tag. It’s impressed some of us here at Android Authority , although others still prefer Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 . The opinion we’re always most interested in is yours — could the iPhone Duo actually tempt everyday Android users to switch sides? We put the question to our readers. The poll appeared in an opinion piece by Dhruv Bhutani, who explained why the iPhone Duo might finally persuade him to abandon Android after 15 years . He’s particularly taken with the phone’s wide design, almost invisible crease, and polished software experience, feeling that Apple has delivered the complete foldable package he’s been waiting for. The cameras are a compromise he’s willing to make, although he wants to try the phone before parting with $2,000. Based on the poll, let’s find out how many of you shared his enthusiasm.

title: Google Translate could soon get its own version of Gboard’s Rambler
summary: Smart assist would clean up your messy speech before translating.
body: TL;DR Google introduced Rambler for Gboard earlier this year, removing filler words and cleaning up your voice input for text conversion. Now Google Translate appears to be preparing its own similar mode called Smart assist. It’s not yet clear if Smart assist would have some of the same limitations as Rambler. Voice-to-text sounds like a great idea… until you actually listen closely to how people really speak. While we expect the written word to be clear and formal, speech is often anything but — and that’s exactly why we have tools like Rambler in Gboard , able to compensate for our messy utterances. Now Google Translate looks like it could be cooking up a similar system of its own. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. title: Apple may have an iPhone 18 Pro demand problem
summary: The new phone apparently isn't selling as well as Apple hoped.
body: TL;DR Apple has reportedly told its suppliers to cut production of components for the iPhone 18 Pro series. New orders have been decreased by at least 15% compared to previous levels, according to reports. This is apparently due to initial iPhone 18 Pro sales failing to meet Apple’s expectations, partly because of its new higher price tag. Apple launched its latest iPhone 18 Pro last month. It’s the most expensive Pro iPhone to date, starting at $1,199 for the smaller model. Maybe not so coincidentally, it’s also reportedly not selling as well as Apple would’ve hoped. As reported by Nikkei Asia (via Reuters ), Apple has been telling suppliers to pull back on production of components used to assemble the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Affected component orders have reportedly been cut by 15% or more.

title: It’s official: Google sets the date for Pixel Watches losing Safety Signal
summary: Mark your calendars for Dec 12, 2026.
body: TL;DR We recently learned that Safety Signal on the Pixel Watch 2 and Pixel Watch 3 LTE is being discontinued, but we didn’t know when. Google has set the end date for Safety Signal and is sending emails and notifications about the changes. A 30-day transition period will begin on the date of the email, after which the service will be inaccessible. Safety Signal for the Pixel Watch 2 and Pixel Watch 3 LTE is exclusively available to Google Health Premium subscribers. Earlier this week, we got some clues that the feature may be going away for good , but didn’t know when. That mystery is now being solved, as Google has officially set a date for Safety Signal’s demise. In a community announcement, Google said it will end support for Safety Signal on December 12, 2026. Current users will be notified by email and push notifications about the change, which will trigger a “30-day transition period.”

title: Amazon admits some of its latest Kindles have a defect (Update: New statement)
summary: Amazon’s Kindle 2026 rollout stumbles as users report light bleed problem.
body: Credit: Amazon TL;DR The base Amazon Kindle 2026 has a light bleed problem. Users are seeing edge shadows or lines of light running along the bezel edges. Amazon admits there was a problem with some batches of the base Kindle, in all colors, and recommends exchanging the device. Update: October 9, 2026 (12:23 PM ET): An Amazon spokesperson has reached out to Android Authority with the following statement: It’s correct that when a device is in dark mode with brightness at max in a dark setting, customers may see a glow around the edges of the book. However, this was expected in order for us to achieve a color bezel, and only appears in certain conditions like when in dark mode with high brightness. If customers want to mitigate this glow, we recommend trying a lower brightness setting when in dark mode.

title: Some Gboard users suddenly can’t type capital letters
summary: The Shift key in Gboard becomes unresponsive, preventing manual capitalization.
body: TL;DR Some Gboard users report that the Shift key randomly stops working, making it impossible to capitalize letters manually. Restarting your phone, force-stopping Gboard, clearing its cache, or switching layouts can temporarily fix it, but it often returns. The issue may be tied to the latest Gboard beta. There are a few things you expect from a smartphone keyboard, beyond just being able to type a capital letter. Autocorrect can misbehave, predictions can get weird, and voice typing can occasionally hear something completely different, but the Shift key? That should just work. Unfortunately, some Gboard users are discovering that even this seemingly bulletproof button can break. Several users have reported that Gboard’s Shift key suddenly stops responding, leaving them unable to capitalize letters manually. A recent Reddit thread has attracted multiple people experiencing the same problem, while other reports today show the issue cropping up on Pixel and Xiaomi devices, though the issue could potentially affect other brands too.

title: Nothing’s audio lineup might soon expand into speakers
summary: An FCC filing for model "E495" hints that the brand could soon launch a portable Bluetooth speaker.
body: Credit: Stephen Radochia / Android Authority TL;DR A new FCC certification listing suggests Nothing is working on a portable wireless speaker with the product code “E495.” While technical details are limited at this stage, the filing confirms Bluetooth connectivity and an integrated rechargeable battery. If and when released, this device would mark the brand’s first venture beyond personal audio into shared listening. Nothing has steadily expanded its footprint across personal audio products, moving from TWS earbuds like the Ear 3a to over-ear headphones like the Headphone 1 Pro . Now, it appears Carl Pei’s design-forward smartphone brand is preparing to enter the wireless speaker space. A fresh FCC certification listing initiated by Nothing reveals a new device with model number “E495.” The FCC listing formally classifies the product as a “Portable Wireless Speaker,” marking it as an entirely new hardware category for the brand.

title: I tested the iPhone 18 Pro’s variable aperture camera. Now I want it on every Android phone
summary: The Android world is missing out.
body: The iPhone 18 Pro offers some interesting lessons for premium Android phones to learn from, such as how to legally ship large batteries and less tangible lessons like how to sell users a narrative . But there’s also one element that Android phones need to relearn from Apple, even though Android pioneered it years ago. A variable camera aperture is barely a feature worth highlighting on a DSLR, but its inclusion on smartphones remains rare. Several Android phones have offered this over the years, but right now the biggest brands in the US and Europe aren’t offering them, leaving a big opportunity for Apple to swoop in.

title: 5 best OnePlus 16 alternatives you can actually buy in the US
summary: OnePlus isn't your only plus-one.
body: With OnePlus pulling out of the North American market , getting your hands on its next flagship will be quite difficult. But that doesn’t mean people have stopped wanting one. title: Users say ‘Gemini as the Google Assistant is a disaster’
summary: Google forced Gemini on Assistant users, and they're not happy about it.
body: Credit: Megan Ellis / Android Authority TL;DR Last month, Google fully removed Google Assistant from all mobile devices. Users have now taken to Reddit to say that Gemini is less reliable than Google Assistant at everyday tasks, including making calls, setting timers, managing alarms, and more. Android Auto navigation problems, missing familiar workflows, and difficulty switching back to Google Assistant are adding to users’ frustration. Many commenters say they want a dependable assistant that follows commands without lengthy explanations. Last month, Google completed its long-running migration from Google Assistant to Gemini by removing the former from all mobile devices and accounts. The company wants Gemini to be the assistant you turn to for everyday tasks on your phone, but many users aren’t convinced the AI is ready to replace Google Assistant.

title: Apple could swiftly follow its smart home event with new iPads and MacBooks
summary: October's heating up for Apple hardware launches, with new iPads now in the running.
body: TL;DR Apple announced its latest iPhones last month, and is planning a smart home event for next week. Those may soon be followed up with a month-end event announcing new MacBook and iPad hardware. In addition to a 14-inch M6-powered iPad, we could see an OLED-equipped iPad mini. With October already upon us, many of the year’s big Android launches already feel like they’re in the rear-view mirror, and we’re increasingly looking forward to 2027 for our next hot hardware fix. But things look very different over on the iPhone side of the fence, and October is quickly shaping up to be a huge one for Apple. We only just got finished hearing about the company’s “Welcome Home” event scheduled for next week , where we expect to meet its big new smart home lineup, and now we’re already learning about what’s next. Apple whisperer Mark Gurman shares over on Bloomberg that Apple plans to follow that smart home event up with another this month, scheduled for October 27. With the new iPhone launch already out of the way, and smart home about to be taken care of, this event would instead focus on new Mac and iPad hardware.

title: Survey suggests a small Android Auto design change is proving surprisingly divisive
summary: It's just a progress bar, isn't it?
body: Credit: Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority Android fans will have noticed that Google seems rather fond of wavy progress bars these days. They’re part of the company’s broader Material 3 Expressive design , and you can find them across Google’s apps and interfaces — including Android Auto . But as we’ve seen the squiggly design make its way to more places, we’ve had less of an idea of what users actually think of it. Until now, that is. Last month, the Android Auto wavy progress bar mysteriously reverted to a straight line for some users , at least when playing music through Spotify in full-screen mode. It wasn’t the first time the feature had disappeared , but it gave us a good excuse to ask readers whether they actually liked the wavy design or preferred the classic straight line. Apparently, a little squiggle can inspire quite a bit of interest, with more than 1,300 readers voting and some surprisingly strong opinions in the comments.

title: AT&T customers are getting surprise password change alerts, but don’t panic yet

body: TL;DR Numerous AT&T subscribers share reports of getting password change emails and texts early this morning. Several of those notifications appear to have gone out at the same time. Right now it doesn’t look like anyone’s actually been compromised, but we’ve reached out to AT&T to confirm. Some emails just ruin your day in a heartbeat: boss requesting a meeting to discuss “restructuring,” landlord notifying you of a rent increase, or just getting some bad news from a family member. High on that list has got to be the surprise “your password has been updated” notification when you never changed anything yourself. Today a whole bunch of AT&T users have been waking up to emails just like that — but it might not be cause for alarm, after all. Over on Reddit’s AT&T sub, we’ve spotted a spate of reports coming in this morning that all describe the same thing: Users getting a message from the carrier in the wee hours of the morning, arriving over both text and email, telling them their password was just changed.

The setup requires an Apple Silicon Mac with at least 16GB of RAM, Xcode Command Line Tools, Android SDK/NDK packages, and 60GB of free space to automatically fetch and build the environment. This Googlebook OS experience on a Max is only intended as an experimental preview rather than a daily driver, as the setup currently has limitations, including broken Bluetooth, a background TPM daemon issue, and a 60Hz display cap. Googlebooks have started reaching the hands of consumers, but not everyone can afford to splurge hundreds of dollars on a new machine, just to see the hype behind Googlebook OS. If you find yourself eager to try out the Android-powered laptop experience and have an Apple Silicon-powered Mac around, you are in luck: a developer has packaged everything required to get Googlebook OS up and running on it and released the entire toolchain publicly. Developer Skylar Taylor-Barrick has shared an open-source toolchain on Reddit and GitHub. Called “ gbos-vm ,” th…

title: Google Maps is launching its own take on the Michelin Guide, and you’re the star
summary: Google Maps is spotlighting 2026's popular eateries and biggest food trends.
body: TL;DR Google Maps is launching its first-ever fan-favorite Dining list, highlighting popular eateries and the biggest food trends across 10 cities worldwide. The annual list draws on Maps reviews, ratings, and directions, with 2026 trends ranging from froyo in New York to dosa in Seattle and hojicha in London. Google is also highlighting its existing weekly Dining lists, Ask Maps restaurant discovery, delivery integrations, and “know before you go” tips. Google Maps has long been handy when you know where you want to eat. The harder question is what to try when you don’t. Google already tackles that through weekly dining lists in Maps’ Explore tab, sorting restaurants into Trending, Gems, and Top collections. Now it’s taking the idea much further by turning a year of Maps activity into its first-ever fan-favorite dining list. Launching today, the new list highlights the year’s biggest food trends and popular eateries across 10 cities worldwide. Google says it built the list from Maps reviews, ratings, and directions, using activity from Maps users to identify the foods and restaurants that broke through in 2026.

title: Creators of Smart Launcher and KWGT are joining hands for something ‘wild’
summary: The merger is called "Wild Pixels," and its first priority is to make both products work better together.
body: Credit: C. Scott Brown / Android Authority TL;DR Smart Launcher and Kustom Industries, the creator of KWGT, are merging to form a new brand called “Wild Pixels.” The collaboration will allow deeper integration between the offerings of the two teams. Details around the upcoming products remain scant, but the duo promises new tweaks and optimizations coming soon. Smart Launcher is one of the many great custom launchers available to Android users . But it offers a few extra features, such as universal search and a custom RSS feed, that make it a tad more intriguing than other available options . Now, Smart Launcher is evolving into something smarter , partnering with another stalwart in the Android space. Smart Launcher is merging with Kustom Industries, the team behind the iconic custom widget creator KWGT , to form a new organization called “ Wild Pixels .” In a joint statement through a Reddit AMA , the two teams said this partnership will allow them to build tighter integrations between their offerings, adding that the partnerships would have been much harder to build separately.
